text:
Recommended design: preregister a factorial ablation crossing loss (BCE, candidate-softmax, gBCE), training-negative count, recent pooling on/off, and candidate-conditioned attention on/off. Keep backbone, training examples, sampler distribution, batch size, optimizer, and checkpoint rule fixed; share negative draws where possible. Include original SASRec and matched-negative gBCE controls: gSASRec changes both loss and negative count, so comparison against one-negative BCE alone cannot attribute gains ([gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192)). Give pooling and attention identical history windows; add parameter-matched candidate-independent attention. Estimate main effects and interactions. Compare equal optimizer updates with equal examples/update for attribution, then equal single-GPU seconds for practical efficiency; charge diagnostics, validation, and failed runs against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

For uncertainty, save each model’s binary HR@10 outcome for every validation user. Adapt [paired bootstrap resampling](https://www.research.ed.ac.uk/en/publications/statistical-significance-tests-for-machine-translation-evaluation/): independently resample 200 users with replacement within each category, reuse identical user indices across models, and compute Δmacro = one-quarter the sum of category mean hit differences. Use 10,000 replicates for a 95% percentile interval; report category differences too. This interval conditions on trained models, four fixed datasets, and fixed candidates; it excludes training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty. Preserve required seeds. Sampled-ranking gains do not establish full-catalog gains ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Repeated checkpoint/hyperparameter selection can overfit these same 800 users ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Preregister contrasts, cap validation looks, log every trial, allocate comparable tuning budgets, and freeze selection before host-held-out evaluation. Post-selection bootstrap intervals remain exploratory; they do not remove winner’s bias. Keep all input splits and the host evaluator unchanged.
